description:
About the Position

The University of Liverpool is advertising a funded doctorate on context-aware metabolite annotation.

It builds on Integrated Probabilistic Annotation to reduce reliance on simple mass matching.

Official Project Title

Advancing Untargeted Metabolomics through a Probabilistic and Context-Aware Annotation Pipeline

Research Focus and Methods

Use language models to curate contextual information, extend analysis across mass-spectrometry platforms and develop an accessible graphical interface. The work links software engineering with metabolomics interpretation.

Research Training and Development

The 3.5-year plan progresses from computational training to platform development and an open-source release.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails
AwardPhD studentship; selection is competitive
ProgrammeLiverpool funded PhD
Duration42 months (3.5 years)
StipendLiving expenses are covered; the advert does not specify a stipend amount.
Tuition and research supportThe advert states that tuition, bench fees and living expenses are covered.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityInternational-equivalent qualifications are accepted; confirm the individual funding and fee-status terms with the supervisor.
Academic preparationFirst-class or high 2:1 degree, or international equivalent, in a quantitative or life-science discipline such as bioinformatics, computing, engineering or biochemistry.
Project interests and skillsStrong computational programming, particularly Python, and interest in AI for biological data.
English languageMeet the host university’s English-language admission rules. An approved alternative or exemption may apply; IELTS is not universally mandatory.

About University of Liverpool

The University of Liverpool is a public research university in Liverpool, England, and a member of the Russell Group. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral study across health, science, engineering, business, humanities and social sciences. Its research and teaching connect specialist expertise with challenges facing communities, industry and society internationally.

Official website: https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/

Application Dates and Location

Deadline, start date and research location
ItemDetails
Application deadlineYear-round applications
Start dateYear-round; agree the start date with the supervisor
Research locationLiverpool, United Kingdom

Contact

  • Email: francesco.del-carratore@liverpool.ac.uk
  • Email: warwick.dunn@liverpool.ac.uk
  • Email: andrew.jones@liverpool.ac.uk

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be sent to the contacts above or raised through the channel given on the official announcement page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Year-round applications - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

  1. Email a CV and cover letter to Dr Francesco Del Carratore to express interest.
  2. If shortlisted, attend the interview and follow the supervisors’ formal submission instructions.
  3. Complete Liverpool’s online application and provide the supporting documents requested in the advert.
  4. Confirm project availability, funding terms and the proposed start date with the supervisor.

Application Checklist

  • CV and cover letter for initial supervisor contact
  • Research proposal and personal statement for the formal application, as requested
  • Academic certificates and transcripts
  • Two referee contacts
  • Passport and English-language evidence where required
